cultural.vision_reason: Classic hand-woven Kente cloth with the characteristic strip-woven checkerboard pattern, oyokoman warp stripes, and zig-zag weft motifs — a textbook Ashanti woman's wrapper.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular woman’s wrapper, composed of 15 hand-woven strips using industrial cotton and rayon, sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are designed and assembled to form a chequerboard pattern; both ends have five bands with a variant design that serves as a border to the main field. Each narrow strip consists of a ground weave that uses in the warp red, yellow and green stripes (the oyokoman pattern) in cotton; the ground warp is in red. In the main field this is crossed by supplementary thread in yellow and black rayon with a uniform pattern of discontinuous zig-zags between continuous blocks, separated by lines of white. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.
